name: dataset/repositories.py
summary: Repository abstraction for Dataset and DatasetTable persistence and query operations
purpose: Encapsulates data access logic for dataset-related models to decouple business rules from Django ORM implementation details, centralizing how Dataset and DatasetTable entities are retrieved, stored, and queried.
responsibilities: Provide CRUD and specialized query operations for Dataset entities
Coordinate persistence and retrieval of related DatasetTable records
Isolate ORM-specific logic from service and domain layers
Enforce data access patterns and query optimizations for the dataset app
inputs: Dataset and DatasetTable model instances or identifiers
Query filters, pagination, and ordering parameters
outputs: Dataset and DatasetTable instances or collections
Persistence operation results and entity states
architecture_notes: Implements the Repository pattern to mediate between the domain and data mapping layers within the dataset app. By importing both Dataset and DatasetTable, it suggests either Dataset acts as an aggregate root with DatasetTable as a child entity, or the repository handles multiple related models. This promotes a layered architecture (service/repository/domain) but risks violating the Single Responsibility Principle if the two models represent distinct business aggregates.
improvements: Clarify aggregate boundaries and split DatasetTable operations into a dedicated repository if it is a separate aggregate root
Introduce an abstract repository interface or protocol to improve testability and support dependency inversion
Add comprehensive type hints and docstrings to all public methods to clarify contracts
Evaluate whether Django custom managers or QuerySets are more idiomatic than explicit repositories unless strict DDD is required
Document transaction boundaries and consider a Unit of Work pattern if operations span multiple repositories
